Subject: Clarifying Commit vs Best Case — field guide + seller lab

Hi team,

As discussed in last week's ops sync, I've pulled together a short field guide that tightens up the Commit / Best Case / Pipeline definitions and includes examples sales can use when updating stages in Salesforce. The goal is explicit rules so we reduce noisy forecast churn and make commit hygiene faster during cadence.

What's attached:
- forecast_field_guide_v3.pdf (definitions + decision tree)
- sellers_lab_invite.ics (30min practice session for reps)

Quick highlights (TL;DR):
- Commit: customer has a signed intent, internal approvals in place, and we have a realistic delivery window (not just a price-sent).
- Best Case: credible close plan but missing 1 of the Commit checks (often legal/PO timing).
- Pipeline: all other opportunities that are active but lacking a confirmed timeline.

Can we run a 30-minute seller lab next week to walk AEs through 4 anonymized example deals and practice tagging? I've penciled in a slot Wed 4/7 10:00am PT — if that time won't work for field, I'll push.

Please skim the guide and reply with any hard no's or additions today so I can finalize before inviting the wider GTM team.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Director, GTM Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is really clear and timely. Two small suggestions inline: 

> Commit: customer has a signed intent, internal approvals in place, and we have a realistic delivery window (not just a price-sent).

Can we add that there must be a named stakeholder who has committed to an internal timeline (I see many "we're waiting on legal" deals where AE still marks Commit)? Suggest: "Commit = signed intent OR documented procurement timeline + named approver."

Also: for the seller lab, recommend we record a 15-min snippet showing the "how to update stage/playbook" in SF (screen capture) for reps who can't make the live session. I can host the examples portion and bring two live opportunity screenshots (anonymized).

If that works, I'm happy for you to finalize and blast to sales.

—Marissa
